mortgageFields.title: Mortgage Details

help.ANNUITY: Your total payment is the same every month. Choose this for a variable-rate mortgage too.
help.CANADIAN_FIXED: A Canadian fixed-rate contract; interest compounds twice a year.
help.LINEAR: The principal part is the same every month and the total falls.
help.INTEREST_ONLY: You pay only interest and the balance does not move.

mortgageFields.termLengthHelp: How long your interest rate or contract term runs, for example a 5-year fixed rate. Monize can remind you before it ends. Leave at 0 years and 0 months for no term.
mortgageFields.paymentFromAccountEditHelp: Changing this moves the upcoming scheduled payments and the payment matching rule to the new account. Payments already posted are not changed.

interestBookingMode.label: How is interest recorded?
interestBookingMode.help: Lets rate detection read your interest correctly. Auto works for most setups.

bookingHelp.title: How to record loan payments
bookingHelp.intro: Each installment has two parts that mean different things in your finances, so record them separately:
bookingHelp.principalBody: It repays borrowed money, not a cost. Record it as a transfer from your bank account to the loan account and leave it uncategorized, so it lowers the loan balance without showing up in expenses or category breakdowns.
bookingHelp.interestBody: It is the real cost of the loan. Record it as an expense with a category (for example "Loans").
bookingHelp.avoid: Avoid: don't record the whole installment as a single expense. It overstates your costs (the real cost is only the interest) and the debt on the loan account never goes down.
bookingHelp.overpayments: Overpayments work like principal: a transfer to the loan account, uncategorized. If the bank added interest to an overpayment, split that part out as a separate expense.

overpaymentRecognition.title: Overpayment recognition
overpaymentRecognition.description: How the schedule tells a standalone overpayment (100% principal) apart from a regular installment. A payment matching any one of these counts as an overpayment.
overpaymentRecognition.memoHelp: Case-insensitive substring match against the payment's memo, its source transaction's memo, or a split memo.

originalPrincipal.label: Original Principal
originalPrincipal.help: The amount you originally borrowed. For an account whose recorded history starts after the mortgage did, this is the amount borrowed, not the opening balance — which is the debt at the start of your history.

prepaymentMode.label: What an Extra Repayment Does
prepaymentMode.SHORTEN_TERM: Shortens the term (same principal each month)
prepaymentMode.help: Check with your lender. After an extra repayment, a statement whose principal part is unchanged means the term was shortened.

detect.toggle: Not sure? Enter a few installments
detect.title: Find your mortgage type
detect.intro: Copy two or three consecutive installments from a statement, oldest first. The balance is optional: with it and the interest rate, Monize can tell whether interest compounds twice a year.
detect.rowIncomplete: Enter both the principal and the interest, or leave the row empty.
detect.rate: Checked against the interest rate entered above, {rate}.
detect.noRate: No interest rate is entered above, so the compounding cannot be checked.
detect.needsFrequency: Choose the payment frequency below first: the installments are read at that cadence.
detect.lowConfidence: Low confidence: check this against your contract or ask your lender before using it.
detect.failed: The installments could not be checked because the request failed. Try again.

reason.TOO_FEW_SAMPLES: At least two consecutive installments are needed to compare.
reason.INVALID_SAMPLE: An installment has a negative or unreadable amount.
reason.NO_PAYMENT: The installments repay no principal and charge no interest.
reason.AMBIGUOUS_CONSTANT_PRINCIPAL_AND_INSTALL: The principal and the total are the same on every installment, which fits a linear and an annuity mortgage alike. Try installments further apart, or check your contract.
reason.ACCELERATED_FREQUENCY: These installments look linear or interest-only, which an accelerated payment frequency cannot be. Check the payment frequency.
reason.NO_RULE_FITS: Neither the principal nor the total stays the same across these installments. If the rate changed between them, use installments from one rate period.
reason.ZERO_PRINCIPAL: No principal is repaid, so the balance does not move.
reason.ZERO_PRINCIPAL_RATE_MISMATCH: No principal is repaid, but the interest is not the quoted rate on the balance. Check the rate.
reason.CONSTANT_PRINCIPAL: The principal part is the same every time and the total falls.
reason.CONSTANT_PRINCIPAL_RATE_MISMATCH: The principal part is the same every time, but the interest is not the quoted rate on the balance. Check the rate.
reason.CONSTANT_INSTALLMENT_SEMI_ANNUAL: The total is the same every time, and the interest matches the quoted rate compounded twice a year.
reason.CONSTANT_INSTALLMENT_NOMINAL: The total is the same every time, and the interest matches the quoted rate without twice-yearly compounding.
reason.CONSTANT_INSTALLMENT_RATE_UNCHECKED: The total is the same every time. Without the balance before each installment and the interest rate, twice-yearly compounding could not be checked.
reason.CONSTANT_INSTALLMENT_COMPOUNDING_AMBIGUO: The total is the same every time, but the balance is too small to tell twice-yearly compounding apart. A Canadian fixed-rate contract says so in its terms.
reason.CONSTANT_INSTALLMENT_RATE_MISMATCH: The total is the same every time, but the interest matches neither convention at the quoted rate. Interest may be charged by the day; check the rate.

interestCategory.title: Interest category
interestCategory.description: Where this loan's interest is recorded. When interest is booked as a separate transaction rather than a split of the payment, naming its category lets the schedule show real interest and lets "Detect from history" find enough interest to work.
interestCategory.label: Interest category

overpaymentCategory.title: Overpayment Detection
overpaymentCategory.description: Recognize standalone overpayments by category, by memo text, or both. Either match counts a payment as 100% principal, so the schedule flags it instead of treating it as a regular installment.
overpaymentCategory.label: Overpayment category
overpaymentCategory.memoHelp: Payments whose memo contains this text count as overpayments (case-insensitive).

notAmortizing.title: This loan does not pay off, so the estimated payoff and remaining interest are unknown.

notAmortizing.beyondHorizon: The installment covers the interest, but the term runs past the projection horizon, so the payoff date and remaining interest are not shown.

simulator.title: Overpayment Simulator

unavailable.title: The overpayment simulation cannot be calculated for this loan yet.
unavailable.reasonPaidOff: This loan has no outstanding balance, so there is nothing left to amortize.
unavailable.reasonNoFrequency: This loan has no payment frequency set. Add it in the account settings.
unavailable.reasonNoRate: This loan has no saved interest rate. Set the interest rate in the account settings, or record a rate change dated today or earlier. A rate shown per row in the schedule below is reconstructed from the interest charged and is not a saved rate.
unavailable.reasonNoPayment: The installment amount cannot be determined. Record the regular installments as transfers to the loan account (principal, with interest as a split line or a separate categorized expense), or set the payment amount in the account settings. Payments booked as ordinary expenses on the source account never reach the loan account, so the schedule cannot see them.
unavailable.reasonNoAmortization: This mortgage has no amortization period, so its installments and its term end cannot be worked out. Set the amortization period in the account settings.
unavailable.reasonNoPaymentStart: This mortgage has no first payment date, so the payments left to its term end cannot be counted. Set up its scheduled payment from the account settings; the first due date you enter becomes payment 1.
unavailable.reasonNoPrincipal: This mortgage has no original amount, so its constant principal cannot be worked out. Set the mortgage amount in the account settings.

simulator.budgetHint: Spend a fixed total on the loan each month; the overpayment is whatever is left after the installment. As the installment falls, the overpayment grows to keep the total the same.
